title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative:
From January 2022, National Productivity and Competitiveness Centre (NPCC) and Kenya National Bureau of Statistics developed a productivity framework and index to improve measurement of productivity. The national productivity framework aims to measure productivity in the public and private sectors and define aspects of performance, efficiency, output, motivation, individual performance, organizational effectiveness, production profitability, cost-effectiveness, competitiveness, and work quality. The Government of Kenya has indicated that the National Productivity and Competitive Framework will be introduced and deployed across Government ministries, departments, and agencies to measure and report on productivity periodically.
ILO supported the designed and delivery in February 2022, a catalytic fund to promote Public Private Development Partnership (PPDP) model. The model is the cooperation between public and private sector actors to proactively create business ventures to improve conditions for people in poverty through skills and lifelong learning to easy access to training in the vocational training centres.
Narok & Nakuru County Governments capacitated to support entrepreneurs in selected economic value chains on village savings group formation, governance, financial records keeping, internal saving and lending. The entrepreneurs were trained on SIYB and practising improved businesses providing jobs to themselves and their workers. With funding from the United States Department of Labour (USDOL) and through the ILO CAPSA Project, the NPCC was financed to convene technical meetings in May and in October 2021. This brought together key State and non-state stakeholders and experts to develop a draft national productivity and Competitive Framework for measuring productivity. ILO continues to support the NPCC to convene consultative meetings of the reference group of experts and stakeholders to finalise the productivity framework and index.
With support from SIDA, which funded the project “Inclusive Growth through Decent Work in the Great Rift Valley ‘’ ILO provided catalytic fund to promote Public Private Development Partnership (PPDP) model. The model is the cooperation between public and private sector actors to proactively create business ventures that also improve conditions for people in poverty through Skills and lifelong learning that facilitate easy access to training in the vocational training centres by the marginalised groups and linkage to the labour market
Through Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (SIDA) funded Inclusive Growth through Decent Work in the Great Rift Valley - KEN/17/01/SWE, ILO trained village saving and lending groups in Narok and Nakuru counties to deliver business and financial services in selected value chains; solar, leather and beads values chains among others; 8 village saving and lending groups with 128 member (93 Female, 35 Males) were trained on group governance, financial records keeping, savings and loaning. They were further trained on value addition and product development in collaboration with 2 vocational training centres. To sustain the support, 45 trainees from 4 partner VTCs were trained on value addition. The project further supported training of 70 entrepreneurs on ILO Improve your Business (IYB) to strengthen record keeping and digital marketing skills
